summary: # Marvelous Designer Quick Start Guide (2023 Update) - Part 10: Application Fabrics ## Introduction In this tutorial video, we use the 11th version of Doshi Marvelous Designer. If you need to learn the 10th version of Marvelous Designer, please watch the previous video. In order to make it easier to learn, Doshi Marvelous Designer is used in this tutorial. We have learned how to create clothing in Marvelous Designer through previous tutorials. Now, we will learn how to make your clothes look more realistic. ## Default Fabric and Fabric Properties You can use default fabric without modifying it. However, by modifying the fabric properties, you can significantly enhance the realism of your clothing. Before starting, open the 3D window to show the thickness and texture of the fabric. Please note that the default fabric is 0.5mm thick. ## Applying Fabric to Clothes Now let's apply the fabric to the clothes: 1. Click on the **Add** button in the fabric window to add a new fabric. 2. Double-click on the name to modify it. 3. Select the adjustment panel tool, then press the **Shift** button to select all the thick and shawl panels. 4. Click on the application button next to the fabric to apply the newly created fabric. When selecting a fabric, the outline of the panel with this fabric will be displayed in orange. Select the new fabric for the T-shirt. You can adjust its properties in the property editor below. ## Adjusting Physical Properties At the bottom of the property editor is the physical property section. You can change the physical properties of the fabric here or select the default fabric provided by Marvelous Designer. When you select a preset fabric, the physical properties below will adjust accordingly. You can also modify these values for manual adjustments. For this tutorial, we will select the preset fabric, which is **Knit Pick Jersey**. Select it and start the simulation. For detailed explanations on physical properties, please refer to other teaching videos on this topic. ## Organizing Panels and Material Settings After changing the physical properties, you can manually organize the panels. Next, let's take a look at the material settings: 1. Choose a different preset type. 2. Add a material pattern to the fabric texture. 3. Adjust the strength of the hairline or change the pattern for the fabric. Click on the color block to change the material color. Regarding transparency, the lower its value, the lighter and more translucent the fabric can be. Please note that the high-quality rendering option in the 3D window of the hook selection can be selected to better check the material effect. However, as a T-shirt, it is still not transparent. ## Importing Preset Fabrics These preset fabrics can also be imported into the library. Let's try to apply a preset fabric to the pocket: 1. Add a new fabric to the fabric window. 2. Select the new fabric. 3. Select the adjustment panel tool and click on the pocket. 4. Click on the application button next to the new fabric to apply it to the panel. Then, open the Fabric folder in the Library window. Here, you can preview the reference effects of various fabrics and drag them onto the fabric to apply these properties. In this video, we will use **lightweight denim** so that you can easily distinguish the materials. When dragging the fabric to the newly created fabric, you will see that the name of the fabric has changed. Double-click to modify it. The fabric dragged in from the Library window will also contain materials and physical properties. You can modify other properties in the property editor. ## Changing Material Type Now, we will change the material type of the fabric to **Fabric Shiny**. Can you feel the difference? Click on the control button to start the simulation. After modifying the material's physical properties, the wearing effect of the clothing will change. The physical properties will affect the stretch of the clothing, the wrinkle texture, etc. Therefore, modifying the appropriate physical properties will help the clothing look more realistic. After changing the material's physical properties, you can adjust the 2D version according to the effect in the 3D window. ## Conclusion Please save your work as a project file, as it will be used in the following courses.
